entries.message: Dragging a pinned tab in a Space whose group shares its pinned tabs works again: the tile lifts under the pointer, the other pins move aside, and it lands where you let go.
A pinned tab you drag stays under the pointer when the window sits at the top of the screen, instead of drawing a row or two below it.

Sidebar folders indent the tabs and folders they hold, a closed folder is as tall as a tab, tabs deep in nested folders keep rounded corners, and opening a folder that holds open folders slides its contents in smoothly.
Opening a folder inside another folder slides its contents in smoothly instead of showing them all at once.
Opening a folder no longer makes the rows below it jump up for a moment before it slides open.
A tab dragged out of a folder keeps its icon and title in place, and dragging several pinned tabs a Sub-Space shares with its group shows them under the pointer.
On iPhone and iPad, a closed folder is as tall as a tab, and its whole row still opens it.
Dragging several selected tabs keeps the icon and title of each tab from inside a folder in place as they lift.
A click on a folder that is closing reaches the row sliding up in its place instead of a tab inside the folder.
Dragging several selected tabs over a window showing another Space no longer offers a Split View there that would not take them.
